_comment: A hook in another harness gates a tool call on it without reading the code: deny is
refused with `reason`, ask goes to a person, allow changes nothing. A decision, rule or
key renamed, or an exit code moved, is therefore a contract change, and this file is the
third point that makes it deliberate: packages/gnomon-cli/src/guard.test.ts asserts the
code's GUARD_DECISIONS / GUARD_RULES / guardExit, the tables in CONTRACTS.md §10 and the
lists here are the same sets, and validates documents the real binary printed against
`verdict_keys`. The per-harness answers (`harness_answers`) are checked the same way.

exit_codes.10: no decision could be made; the document says decision ask, rule error, and why in `error`

project_sources._comment: Where `.gnomon/` is found when the call's working directory is in no governed project (a host shell moved out of it by `cd`, or into a nested repository): each host's own project root (CONTRACTS.md §10 'Which project'). A working directory inside a governed project is judged there.

hook_agents._comment: The --agent each hook `gnomon guard install` writes passes (for the opencode plugin, its default; $GNOMON_GUARD_AGENT overrides it). The guard maps it to a role through [check.roles] in .gnomon/policy.toml. With no entry there, or one naming no declared role, it has no role and answers every call ask (rule error, 'no role'). install warns on stderr with the [check.roles] line to add, and exits as before; guard status lists such a hook in `warnings`, not `findings` (#205, CONTRACTS.md §10).
